transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-16
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood SE), Maya Rao (Aurora ML), Ethan Li (Aurora Eng), Priya Menon (Aurora PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Samira opened with hosted API capabilities for vector search + reranking; Jonas demoed embeddings endpoint, search flow, and the reranker endpoint. Aurora asked about latency vs cost, cold-starts, prefix caching (KV cache), and SSO/KMS controls. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with prioritized queries and an SLO report.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint, Console search walkthrough, Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/caching/quantization), security (SOC2, SSO), pilot scope and success metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? We got about 45 minutes, want to show an end-to-end hosted flow for vector retrieval + rerank and then talk pilot scope.
[00:12] Maya (Aurora): Hi, Maya here, ML lead. We're particularly interested in improving search relevance for our knowledge base — lots of product docs and support transcripts.
[00:18] Ethan (Aurora): Ethan — infra/eng. Focused on latency and cost, we run queries at peak and need predictable tail latency.
[00:25] Priya (Aurora): Priya, product. Will own success metrics.
[00:30] Jonas (Redwood SE): Great — I'll jump into the console demo after Samira's quick overview. High level: hosted embeddings + reranker lets you keep embeddings and reranks in our managed service, no infra on your side. You can call embeddings for indexing and our search+rerank endpoints for a two-stage flow.
[00:48] Samira (Redwood): Right — quick clarify, Aurora, do you plan to store vectors in Redwood or continue with an existing vector DB?
[00:55] Maya (Aurora): We currently use an in-house vector store built on Faiss, but it's getting expensive and we want to try a managed path for quality experiments first.
[01:05] Jonas (Redwood): Totally. You can keep Faiss for the initial coarse retrieval and call our reranker to rescore top-k, or you can migrate indexing to Redwood's hosted vectors. Both patterns are common.
[01:20] Ethan (Aurora): If we keep Faiss, do we need to push raw text or vectors to Redwood to rerank?
[01:27] Jonas (Redwood): For rerank we accept either: you can send the context passages + query and we do a cross-attention rerank; or send candidate vectors and minimal metadata if you want a vector-only pipeline. The cross-attention rerank is better for precision but more expensive/latency-sensitive.
[01:45] [00:01:50] Speaker 1: sorry can you repeat the cross-attention bit?
[01:52] Jonas (Redwood): Yeah, cross-attention means the model jointly encodes query+document which yields higher relevance signals (phrasing match, implicit entailment). It usually costs more tokens and compute vs a dot-product score but improves top-1/top-3.
[02:10] Maya (Aurora): What's the typical latency for a cross-attention rerank on hosted? We're aiming for p95 < 220ms end-to-end on simple queries.
[02:18] Jonas (Redwood): Good target. For single passage rerank on our medium models, typical p95 is 60-120ms when routed to low-latency pools; but end-to-end will depend on your first-stage retrieval. If you pass 10 candidates to rerank, rerank cost scales linearly.
[02:35] Hannah (Redwood): We also have batching and smart KV cache (we're seeing customers call it K-V cash in transcripts) that helps repeated prefixes and can cut cost by 20-40% on stable workloads.
[02:48] Ethan (Aurora): That KV cache — is it available on hosted? Any guarantees about cache eviction or warm-up?
[02:55] Jonas (Redwood): Yes, hosted has prefix and KV caching; eviction is LRU-ish but you can pin certain keys in Dedicated. Warm-up is workload dependent; Optimize will suggest batch windows and cache TTLs based on your query distribution.
[03:10] Priya (Aurora): Can you show the console flow — creating an embeddings index, running a sample search, and then plugging in reranker?
[03:18] Jonas (Redwood): Sure, switching screens — console.app/redwood demo.
[03:22] [03:23] Jonas (Redwood): (screen) Here is the embeddings tab — you can upload CSV or call the embeddings API directly. We show token-level cost estimates and model perf profiles; I'm going to index a small doc set we preloaded for this demo.
[03:40] Jonas (Redwood): Creating index... choosing model: "redwood-emb-1" (opt for cheaper/dense vectors) vs higher-dim options for recall. You can set vector dims and hybrid fields.
[03:52] Maya (Aurora): Hybrid fields?
[03:54] Jonas (Redwood): Yes, you can store structured metadata to filter on (product version, doc type) and do vector + filter queries in the Console.
[04:02] [04:05] Samira (Redwood): Quick security note — hosted is SOC 2 compliant, SSO via SAML/Okta, and you can enforce KMS for any optional private key storage. For regulated data we often recommend Redwood Private, but many customers run sensitive KBs on hosted with tokenization + audit logs.
[04:22] Ethan (Aurora): Do you log full inputs? We have concerns about PII and retention.
[04:28] Samira (Redwood): By default we retain inputs for 14 days for debugging but you can opt out or configure retention; enterprise seats can push audit logs to a customer-owned log sink. We'll send the security checklist; Jonas has the SOC2 link.
[04:42] Jonas (Redwood): Back to demo, I'm running a sample search — query: "how to reset API tokens for legacy clients". First-stage returns 200 candidates (we limit to top-k 100 for UI), then we select top 10 and call the reranker endpoint.
[05:00] [05:05] Jonas (Redwood): (typing) Calling /search with embeddings: hits show score and snippet. Now calling /rerank with 10 docs — watching latency... 85ms. You can see top doc moved from rank 3 to rank 1 after rerank.
[05:20] Maya (Aurora): Nice. The snippet match is much better after rerank. How are rewrites or canonicalization handled? We have messy transcripts with shorthand.
[05:30] Jonas (Redwood): We have optional normalization layers — you can pre-process text with our tokenization helpers or send normalized fields. Also Optimize suggests prompt templates and paraphrase-robust rerank prompts.
[05:45] Ethan (Aurora): Cost — how should we think about cost if we rerank every query?
[05:50] Samira (Redwood): Typical pattern: coarse recall cheap (local Faiss or hosted ANN) + rerank only top-N. Optimize provides per-route cost estimates; you can set fallback policies (e.g., skip rerank during heavy load or use a cheaper model).
[06:06] Priya (Aurora): For our SLA we need degraded mode — prefer latency over absolute precision during peaks. Can we auto-fallback?
[06:12] Jonas (Redwood): Yep, smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks: route to cheaper model or skip rerank, and we emit an expose metric so you can alert on fallback rates.
[06:24] [06:30] Speaker 2: who handles rate limits?
[06:32] Samira (Redwood): Rate limits can be set at the API key or account level; Dedicated customers can set much higher caps and we have quota bursting.
[06:40] Maya (Aurora): On private data residency: our legal asks for EU-only processing for EU customers. Can hosted restrict region?
[06:48] Samira (Redwood): Hosted can pin the region; we have EU-region clusters. For stricter residency or on-prem controls we'd look at Redwood Private. We'll include region options in the follow-up.
[06:58] Jonas (Redwood): Quick aside on reranker prompt patterns — we often use a contrastive prompt that asks the model to score documents 1-5 with short rationale. That gives structured signals that feed into downstream UI.
[07:15] Maya (Aurora): Can you share examples later?
[07:17] Jonas (Redwood): Yes, I'll include prompt examples and an evaluator harness.
[07:20] [07:25] Jonas (Redwood): Now switching to the API triflow: call embeddings endpoint -> index/store -> first stage search -> call rerank. Demonstrate curl snippets...
[07:32] Jonas (Redwood): (reads) curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"..."}' - you'll get vector blob. Then /search accepts query vector or text, and /rerank accepts a list of docs and query.
[07:45] Ethan (Aurora): Any SDKs? We prefer Python and Go.
[07:48] Hannah (Redwood): We have Python, Node, and a Go client in beta. The Python client has first-class helpers for batch embeddings and streaming rerank responses.
[07:58] Maya (Aurora): For throughput — we ingest about 1.2M docs and 30k queries/day, bursty. Is hosted going to be cheaper than us running Faiss on EC2?
[08:12] Samira (Redwood): Hard to say without your access patterns. Often managed hosting reduces ops and improves tail latency; Optimize can show projected cost savings after we analyze your token mix and QPS. For very large corpus some customers combine Redwood for rerank and use their own ANN for coarse retrieval.
[08:30] [08:35] Priya (Aurora): For pilot, we want a sample of 10k docs and production-like query stream. Can Redwood handle that scale in a 2-week pilot?
[08:42] Jonas (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll set up a sandbox project, provide sample ingestion scripts and a small performance harness to replay queries. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, cost per query, and rerank lift (mrr/ctr as you define).
[08:58] Maya (Aurora): What about model drift — if rerank model updates change behavior, can we pin versions?
[09:05] Hannah (Redwood): Yes, model pinning and rollouts are supported. You can pin to a specific model revision in the route and do canary rollouts with metrics comparison. Optimize will also track quality regressions on your eval set.
[09:22] Ethan (Aurora): Do you support embeddings dimensionality changes without re-indexing everything?
[09:28] Jonas (Redwood): Changing vector dims typically requires reindexing. We support hybrid indexes (store both old and new) but reindex is standard. We can provide reindex helpers.
[09:38] [09:45] Maya (Aurora): Encryption at rest? Key management?
[09:48] Samira (Redwood): AES-256 at rest; customer-managed keys via KMS is available for enterprise/private. We'll attach KMS integration docs.
[09:58] [10:02] Jonas (Redwood): Demo note: I'm going to show rerank latency under a small QPS blast — sending 20 concurrent rerank requests to show tail.
[10:10] Jonas (Redwood): (typing) launching load... p50 42ms, p95 130ms, p99 240ms for 10-candidate rerank on the small model. If you parallelize rerank for more candidates you'll see linear increases, but we also support candidate batching tricks.
[10:30] Maya (Aurora): The p99 is tricky for our SLO. Any mitigations?
[10:34] Jonas (Redwood): You can gate concurrency on your side or use our Dedicated pool for tighter tail guarantees. Also model quantization reduces memory pressure and lowers variance. Optimize can recommend a quantization profile per model for your latency targets.
[10:50] Ethan (Aurora): Are there public perf numbers?
[10:54] Samira (Redwood): We publish model perf profiles in the Console and can share a perf spreadsheet. I'll include the public benchmark link.
[11:05] [11:10] Priya (Aurora): Let's talk acceptance criteria for pilot — what metrics should we capture?
[11:14] Jonas (Redwood): I'd propose: 1) rerank lift: MRR increase vs baseline, 2) latency: p95 end-to-end under 250ms for typical queries, 3) cost per query within X% of projection, 4) false positive rate on sensitive content should be zero and data retention configured.
[11:30] Maya (Aurora): We'll add click-through improvement and support deflection rate.
[11:34] Samira (Redwood): Good. We'll define the pilot runbook in the follow-up.
[11:40] [11:50] Speaker 3: quick question about A/B testing flow?
[11:52] Hannah (Redwood): Console supports route-level A/B tests: you can split traffic between rerank on/off or rerank-model-A/model-B and we bucket responses and provide per-route metrics.
[12:04] Ethan (Aurora): Integration overhead — how many engineer-weeks to get to pilot?
[12:09] Samira (Redwood): For a 10k doc pilot with our ingestion scripts and one eng point-person, most customers get a running pilot in 2-5 days of lift. We'll provide an onboarding runbook.
[12:20] Maya (Aurora): Any gotchas with our data — transcripts have timestamps, speaker labels, and many short-lines. Does that affect embeddings quality?
[12:28] Jonas (Redwood): Short lines are fine; we recommend chunking and enriching with metadata (speaker, timestamp) so rerank can prefer more complete answers. Optimize can suggest chunk sizes.
[12:40] [12:45] Priya (Aurora): Legal will ask for DPA and security docs.
[12:48] Samira (Redwood): We'll attach DPA, SOC2 report, and a data flow diagram for your legal team.
[12:55] Maya (Aurora): One more — can rerank produce explanations or rationales we can show in UI?
[13:02] Jonas (Redwood): Yes — rerank can return short rationale strings if you enable the explain flag; it's a tiny token overhead but helpful for trust. We also have structured score breakdowns (semantic-match, recency, metadata).
[13:18] Ethan (Aurora): Fractional billing — if we only rerank some queries, can we get per-route cost breakdown?
[13:25] Hannah (Redwood): The Console has per-route token/cost breakdown and we expose per-request cost in headers for programmatic accounting.
[13:34] [13:40] Samira (Redwood): Alright, time check — 10 minutes left. Quick recap and next steps.
[13:45] Samira (Redwood): Action items: Samira sends pricing + DPA, Jonas shares rerank prompt examples and benchmark harness, Aurora to send internal success metrics and a small sample of queries. Schedule pilot kickoff for next week.
[14:02] Maya (Aurora): Sounds good. Any blockers from your side?
[14:07] Samira (Redwood): No blockers — we'll need a technical contact (Ethan) and PM contact (Priya) to sign off pilot scope.
[14:15] Priya (Aurora): I'll own product-side signoff.
[14:18] Ethan (Aurora): I'll work with Jonas on ingestion.
[14:22] [14:30] Jonas (Redwood): I'll follow up with a runbook and the sample scripts. Expect links to the Console sandbox and a small benchmark harness.
[14:38] Samira (Redwood): Thanks everyone. We'll send follow-up email with links and proposed dates.
[14:45] Maya (Aurora): Thanks — appreciate the walkthrough.
[14:47] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription occasionally labeled Speaker 1/2 and conflated KV cache as K-V cash; some technical terms mis-transcribed (quantization -> quantize-ation) — we've left them as-is to reflect raw export.
